sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:164248
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 34477 of 2023

Applicant :- Ravikant
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Hare Krishna Tripathi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri H.K. Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Jhamman Ram, learned AGA for the State.
3. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 144 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Tahrauli,
District Jhansi during pendency of the trial.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and his family members and according to the FIR marriage of the applicant was performed with the deceased in the month of April, 2018 and after marriage applicant and his family members tortured the deceased for motorcycle and informant received an information with regard to her daughter i.e. deceased and when he arrived at spot then found that his daughter i.e. deceased has died.

Ravikant vs State Of U.P. on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147914934/
1 5.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation of demand of dowry and torture made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and only being husband of the deceased, applicant has been falsely implicated in the present matter.

He further submits that in the FIR as well as in the statement of witnesses recorded during investigation, it appears that there was allegation of torture and demand of dowry but when informant i.e. father of the deceased and her mother appeared before the trial court and their statements were recorded by trial court then they have declared hostile and they stated that there was no demand of dowry and deceased died due to illness.
6. He further submits that actually deceased committed suicide as she was having some problem related to Ghost.
He further submits that even autopsy report of the deceased suggests that she died due to hanging.
He further submits that applicant in the present matter is in jail since 08.09.2022.

7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within four years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home and there is also allegation of demand of dowry and applicant very casually stated that his wife died due to problem of shadow of ghost, therefore, he failed to explain the death of his wife.

He further submits that although father and mother of the deceased were declared hostile but from their statements it appears that they have won over by the applicant and they very casually stated that due to stomach pain deceased died and there is difference with regard to death of the deceased in the averment of applicant and her parents, therefore, applicant should not be released on bail.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. Although, from the record it reflects that informant i.e. father of the deceased and her mother during trial have declared hostile but applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within four years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home and initially there was allegation of demand of dowry against the applicant and his family members and in paragraph-26 applicant stated that deceased died because she was suffering with ghost problem,
therefore, I find force in the argument advanced by learned AGA that vague defence has been taken by the applicant and applicant failed to explain the death of his wife.

10. Further, from the statement of the parents of the deceased recorded before the trial court, it appears that they have stated that deceased died due to stomach pain and story narrated by the parents of the deceased also appears to be quite improbable and I find force in the argument advanced by learned AGA that it appears that they have won over by the applicant.
11.

Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
12. Accordingly, the instant bail application is rejected.

Ravikant vs State Of U.P. on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147914934/
2 13.

However, considering the fact that applicant in the present matter is in jail since September,
2022 and parents of the deceased have declared hostile, trial court is directed to conclude the trial within six months from the date of production of certified copy of this order strictly under the provisions of Section 309 Cr.P.C. without granting unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties,
if there is no legal impediment.

14. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 16.8.2023 AK Pandey  Ravikant vs State Of U.P. on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147914934/
